text.p: An international donors' conference aimed at raising $1.4 billion for Bosnia's reconstruction has been postponed for the second time this year, a World Bank official said on Wednesday.

The conference should have been held in March but was postponed until April to give the Bosnian government time to adopt economic reforms and clinch a deal with the International Monetary Fund (IMF). Now the April date will also be missed.

"It seems that since the IMF programme is not yet fully finalised, the chance of an April conference looks most unlikely. It won't take place in April," the World Bank's Sarajevo director Rory O'Sullivan told Reuters.

International officials have urged Bosnia's central government, comprised of representatives of the former warring Serb, Croat and Moslem factions, to adopt a set of economic laws and clinch a deal with the IMF.
Before committing funds to Bosnia, foreign donors want to see Bosnia sign an agreement with the IMF, which in turn wants to see a functioning central bank and budget laws in place.

Servicing Bosnia's foreign debt and tariff laws are also a part of a so-called "quick-start package" proposed by international officials in order to satisfy donors' demands for building a self-sustainable economy.
But political bickering has impeded reform enactment and western negotiators' patience has begun wearing thin.
O'Sullivan said some progress was made on IMF issues over the last week, giving confidence that the conference could be on track for the next date.

"(The postponement) is sending a message that the donors' community is very, very serious about the need for structural reform in the Bosnian economy as a precondition for very substantial investment," he said.
Bosnia's 3-1/2 year war ended with a U.S.-brokered peace accord in 1995 and international community said it would pledge $5.1 billion over three to four years for priority reconstruction.
